# Change Log — Forge Engine activity history

Machine-readable history of engine changes. A future interactive history page will render the
JSON array below; agents maintain it by hand until then.

## Maintenance rules (agents: follow these)

- Append a `change` entry for every file you create, modify, or delete: one entry per file, with
  the `model` that made the edit (`modelVersion` when known, else `null`), the `file` path, and a
  brief `what` + `why`.
- Before each PR merge, append a `pr-merge` entry summarising **all** changes in that PR.
- Entries are chronological (oldest first). `id` is zero-padded sequential — use last id + 1.
- `model` is the agent identity as known to the session. Arena sessions use `"Arena Agent Mode"`
  unless the specific underlying model is known, in which case record it (and its version).
- After editing, validate the block still parses: `node -e '...'`
  (extract the ```json fence and `JSON.parse` it — see `tools/` if a checker exists by then).

## Entry schemas

`change`: `id, date (UTC ISO), type, pr (number|null), branch, model, modelVersion, file, what, why`
`pr-merge`: `id, date (UTC ISO), type, pr, branch, base, title, model, modelVersion, summary, files[]`
(`note` is optional on any entry.)

HighGainAntennaController arms on GLB load, unfurls 5 s later at a 40\u00b0/s slew, then re-solves Earth in gimbal space every frame at 70\u00b0/s with elevation clamped 12\u00b0\u201385\u00b0; one-way, no stow control anywhere; the assembly is procedural (post, two pivots, dish, feed) because the NASA GLB ships no HGA. 26 new tests (envelope, reduction, top-speed regression, regen, wheel anchoring, antenna contract); the browser gate drives the rover (dz 0.54 m, kick dust, HGA deploying, 0 GPU errors). 501 tests in 38 files; verify, lint:arch, docs:check, check:browser all green.",

    "what": "New: the clustered-lighting builder. A 16x8x24 view-space grid (3072 clusters) indexes up to MAX_CLUSTERED_LIGHTS=256 local lights; each light's view-space bounding box is projected at both of its depths, its log slice range widened by one, near/far/off-frame lights culled, and a cluster over MAX_LIGHTS_PER_CLUSTER=32 evicts its least influential lights (intensity x Rec.709 luma) and reports it. Writes a flat cluster-major index list into reused typed arrays: nothing allocated per build.",
    "why": "Phase 13.3. The frame's light cap was a fixed 16-entry uniform list that writeLights truncated silently; a per-fragment list of only the lights that can reach it lifts the cap to 256 and makes the shader's cost follow the lights near a pixel instead of the lights in the scene."

    "why": "The grid's quantisation and its two arrays have to be generated layouts, not hand-written WGSL, or the CPU writer and the shader drift apart. Both blocks are far past (or need not fit) the 64 KiB uniform binding limit, so they are storage-bound and needed their own registry."

    "summary": "Phase 13.3 clustered (Forward+) lighting. Generated ClusterUniforms/ClusterLightBlock/ClusterGridBlock on frame bindings 6-8 (~428 KB resident, only the used prefixes uploaded), perFrame.flags bit 5, EngineConfig/SceneSettings switches (off on minimal/low), seven new stats plus Renderer.clusterBuildInfo, and demo Clustered / +36 lamps buttons with a HUD lights line. Two bugs only the real GPU could see became CPU gates: WGSL's reserved words (the grid's offset array shipped as `meta`, which Tint rejects at parse time \u2014 every pipeline came back invalid and every frame failed to submit, while the mock device, check:wgsl and 537 unit tests stayed green because none of them compile WGSL) are now rejected by validateWgsl; and projecting a light's box at its nearest depth only is not conservative, because ndc.x = proj*x/z moves toward the centre as z grows, which cost an off-axis lamp the inner crescent of its own pool (181 darker px) \u2014 it is now projected at both depths and pinned by a 2 cm walk of the ground that fails on the old code (1,986 misses to 0 over 145,323 CPU probes).     "branch": "arena/01a0d87a-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/clusters.ts",
    "what": "Each cluster now owns MAX_LIGHTS_PER_CLUSTER consecutive slots of the index list instead of an (offset, count) pair, so the per-cluster cap *is* the stride and `capFit` is gone; `build` is split into `prepare` (ranges: spheres, near/far/off-frame culls, tile and slice extents), `count` (the lists' lengths and the frame's aggregates, from the per-slice difference plane) and `fill` (the lists themselves); `packRanges`/`influenceOf`/`RANGE_KEY_BITS` pack one u32 key plus one influence rank per light.",
    "why": "The packed layout needed a prefix sum, so any other producer of the grid would have had to run a scan pass before it could write a single list, and capFit could silently shrink the cap when a scene used every cluster. Splitting the build separates the coverage-independent half (count: exact lengths, aggregates, what the fragment stage indexes with) from the coverage-proportional half (fill: what the GPU is there for), which is what makes both the GPU rasteriser and the reported stats possible."
  },

    "what": "New: the GPU fill (Phase 13.4). `LIGHT_CULL_SHADER` generates `csAssign` (one invocation per cluster, one workgroup per 256; coverage test from the packed keys, eviction of the least influential light at the cap, insertion-sort back into light order after an eviction) plus its bindings, from the generated layout structs and RANGE_KEY_BITS; `coversKey` is the coverage decode in TypeScript, `assignClustersOnCpu` is the shader's algorithm in TypeScript (the executable spec the tests pin), and `GpuLightCuller` uploads the frame's ranges (prefix only: 2 KB max, 4 B when nothing clustered), builds one pipeline and one bind group, and records `forge.lights.assign` as a side-effect pass.",
    "why": "The fill is the only stage whose cost grows with coverage (14.1 ms for a 256-lamp rig on one thread) and the only one a single CPU thread cannot widen; the counting pass stays on the CPU because its output is needed exactly and immediately. Doing the fill on the device also means the light-index blocks are never uploaded, and nothing needs reading back: the aggregates are functions of the counts."
  },

    "what": "ClusterRangeEntry (packed key + influence) and ClusterRangeBlock (count + 256 entries, 2052 B, storage-only) added to the registries, so the shader embeds generated declarations instead of a hand-written copy.",
    "why": "The range block is the CPU\u2192GPU interface for the assignment pass: the WGSL decode and `packRanges` have to agree bit for bit, and the way this repo keeps two languages in step is to generate the struct once and assert the shader text contains it verbatim."
  },

    "pr": 42,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d87a-forge-engine",
    "base": "main",
    "title": "Phase 13.4: the device fills the cluster grid (GPU light assignment)",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "summary": "Phase 13.4: the device fills the cluster grid. The cluster build splits into three stages with three cost curves \u2014 prepare is O(lights), count is O(lights x slices + clusters) (a per-slice difference plane, so a lamp sweeping the grid costs the same corner writes as one in a single tile), and the fill (the lists) is O(coverage). Only the fill was worth moving: benchmarks/src/lights.bench.ts measures the demo-shaped rig at ~0.5 ms / 7,749 entries and a saturating rig (256 lamps, every cluster) at 50-75 ms / 98,304 entries = 3,072 clusters x the 32-entry cap, against 0.04-0.09 ms for the same frames' counting pass. prepare and count stay on the CPU because their output is needed exactly and immediately (the fragment stage indexes with counts, stats reports them, lightsDropped is a correctness signal) and neither grows with coverage; nothing is read back, so clustersUsed / clusterIndices / maxLightsPerCluster / lightsDropped are the CPU's own numbers for the same frame. The pass is forge.lights.assign, first in the frame (shadow/prepass never read the grid, forge.main's fragment stage does), one invocation per cluster in 12 workgroups of 256, reading the frame's packed ranges (ClusterRangeBlock, 2 KB; each light's tile/slice extents packed into one u32 by RANGE_KEY_BITS) and the grid's own counts, writing at most counts[c] entries per cluster so a wrong count trims a list instead of spilling into the next one; the shader is a transcription of the CPU fill (same light order, same intensity x Rec.709 luma eviction with ties keeping the earlier light, same re-sort), and assignClustersOnCpu is its TypeScript twin, pinned byte for byte by tests/lightCulling.test.ts including saturated lists. The grid block became fixed-stride (counts + indices, CLUSTER_COUNT x MAX_LIGHTS_PER_CLUSTER = 98,304 u32, 405,504 B; ~416 KB resident) and RendererOptions.lightCulling = auto|cpu|gpu with stats.clusterFill and the demo's ?lightculling=cpu|gpu plus HUD drive it. Two bugs, both invisible to the CPU gates: Tint rejects a shift mixed with a comparison without parentheses (a *parse* error that invalidated every pipeline built from the module while the mock, check:wgsl and 537 tests stayed green), so the generated decode is ((key >> shift) & mask)u and validateWgsl (mixedOperatorIssues) now fails on that shape on the CPU side; and switching the fill to \"cpu\" disposed the GpuLightCuller but kept the reference, so the ??= reused a dead culler whose record() returns immediately \u2014 forge.lights.assign silently vanished after a cpu->gpu round trip (19 passes -> 18, while stats.clusterFill still said \"gpu\") and the grid was never refilled, which the real device showed as ~110k pixels darker in tile-shaped bands on the demo's 36-lamp rig. The setter now clears the field, tests/frame.test.ts pins the round trip, and check:browser asserts the pass is back in the frame before it reads a pixel, that the gpu arm owns the pass while the cpu arm lacks it, that the many-light frame is strictly brighter than the truncated uniform path with no pixel darker, and that the two fills agree over the fixture and past the per-cluster cap (a 40-lamp ball at the origin, where only the eviction path runs). That last section had never executed before this PR's culler fix \u2014 the many-light assertion upstream threw on every run \u2014 and it failed on a reversed pixel comparison (compareLuma counts the *second* argument brighter; the check asked for idle-vs-rig and so reported the rig's own 2,434 px as \"darker\"), now fixed and paired with an assertion that the rig can never remove light. Verified on a real device: fill handover back in the frame, many-light 81,499-88,596 px brighter with none darker, fill A/B 0 px differ with the pass owned by the gpu arm, stacked rig 2,414-2,434 px brighter with cap 32 reached and no cpu-vs-gpu difference; 565 tests in 41 files, bench guards, lint:arch, check:testmap, docs:check all green. rendering.gpuLightCulling verified; rendering.clusterCoverage deferred (perspective-only, 256/32 caps, ~416 KB resident \u2014 the roadmap schedules no work for it).",

  {
    "id": "0176",
    "date": "2026-09-25T20:40:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d9e9-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/uniforms.ts",
    "what": "New 13.5 blocks: `ObjectUniforms` gains `visibilityIndex` (and a `_pad`, 176 B); `ObjectCullUniforms` (240 B: view/proj/viewProj, cameraPos, near/far, extent, batchCount, flags, hizLevels) and the storage-only `ObjectBatchEntry` (32 B: AABB min/max, min.w = the batch's distance limit), `ObjectBatchBlock` (8192 entries, 262144 B) and `ObjectCullStatsBlock` (four `atomic<u32>` counters, 16 B), plus `MAX_CULLED_BATCHES`; both new storage structs registered in `RENDERING_STORAGE_STRUCTS` so `check:wgsl` validates them in the storage space.",
    "why": "The culler needs one word per batch (`visibilityIndex`), the frame's own matrices to extract planes from on the device, and one bounds entry per batch whose limit travels with the box because batches merge by geometry/material rather than by distance.",
    "note": "`ObjectCullStatsBlock`'s fields are `atomic<u32>`, not `u32`: `atomicAdd(ptr<storage, u32, read_write>, u32)` has no overload, and a plain `u32` compiled happily on the mock while Tint rejected `objects.cull` on a real device."
  },
  {
    "id": "0177",
    "date": "2026-09-25T20:40:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d9e9-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/gpu/layout.ts",
    "what": "New `atomicU32` `FieldType` (4 bytes, emits `atomic<u32>`) and a `uniformLayoutProblems` rule that rejects it in the uniform address space. `alignOf`/`sizeOf`/`wgslType` handle it.",
    "why": "WGSL only allows atomics in the storage address space, so the struct generator has to be able to say `atomic<u32>` \u2014 and only there. The registry then keeps its promise that a struct it emits for `uniform` is legal in that space.",
    "note": "The first real-device run of Phase 13.5 is what surfaced this: `check:wgsl`, the mock device and 584 tests were all green on a `u32` counter block that no GPU would compile."
  },
  {
    "id": "0178",
    "date": "2026-09-25T20:40:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d9e9-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/objectCulling.ts",
    "what": "New module: `cullPlanesFrom` (the same six planes `Frustum.setFromViewProjection` derives, unnormalized), `cullBatchesOnCpu` (the shader's twin: frustum sphere test, per-batch distance limit, HiZ rectangle + texel walk), `buildHizOnCpu`/`hizLevelCount`/`hizLevelSize` (view-space-metre pyramid, 2x2 max per level), `HIZ_DEPTH_SHADER`/`HIZ_REDUCE_SHADER`/`OBJECT_CULL_SHADER` (generated from the structs and constants, one invocation per batch, `atomicAdd` into the counters), and `GpuObjectCuller` (pipelines, bounds/stats/HiZ buffers, per-frame `hizLevelsFrame`, `mapAsync` readback of the counters one frame late, `dispose`).",
    "why": "Phase 13.5: decide batch visibility on the device (frustum, per-batch distance, HiZ occlusion), with a CPU twin the mock device can run so every CPU gate still sees real verdicts.",
    "note": "Two real-device bugs found here, both invisible to the CPU gates: a depth texture's `textureLoad` needs the mip level explicitly (Chromium accepts the two-argument form, Tint does not), and the HiZ pixel row is the negated NDC y (texel row 0 is the top) \u2014 the mirrored rectangle tested the other half of the screen and culled floating geometry against the ground below it."
  },
  {
    "id": "0179",
    "date": "2026-09-25T20:40:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d9e9-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/renderer.ts",
    "what": "13.5 wiring: `RendererOptions.objectCulling` (auto/cpu/gpu) and `occlusionCulling`; `RenderStats.cullTested`/`cullFrustum`/`cullDistance`/`cullOccluded`; `Batch.maxDistance` (merged batches keep the most permissive member's); `reserveObject(matrix, count, visibilityIndex)`; `prepareObjectCulling` (bounds staging, mode decision, word zeroing, twin or device prepare); `ensureVisibilityCapacity` (256-byte-aligned growth that drops the draw bind group); the cull passes recorded between the prepass and the SSAO chain; `pollObjectCulling()` after execution; `objectCulling` and `occlusionCulling` accessors (the cpu setter disposes the culler and clears the reference); `syncGraphEpoch` invalidates the culler's cached views; `dispose` releases culler + visibility buffer.",
    "why": "The renderer owns the batches, the bounds and the visibility buffer the draw layout binds; the culler owns everything else. Reading `occlusionCulling` through a field (not `options`) lets the demo and the browser gate flip it per frame.",
    "note": "The accessors mirror `lightCulling`'s trap: a disposed culler records nothing, so a stale reference would leave every later frame without a cull pass while `stats` still claimed the device path. The file also had a doc comment for the prepass's group 0 misplaced above `prepareObjectCulling` (its builder is `ensurePrepassBindGroup`); it was moved to its own member."
  },
  {
    "id": "0180",
    "date": "2026-09-25T20:40:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d9e9-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/pipeline.ts",
    "what": "`drawLayout` gains group 1 binding 2 (`visibility`, vertex stage, read-only storage, `minBindingSize: 4`).",
    "why": "The batch's vertex stage reads its visibility word to collapse the clip position of a culled batch; without the binding the shader would not compile, and `minBindingSize: 4` is what makes a grown buffer visible to the pipeline at all."
  },
  {
    "id": "0181",
    "date": "2026-09-25T20:40:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a0d9e9-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/shaders/standard.ts",
    "what": "`BINDINGS.visibility` (group 1, binding 2), `batchVisibility: array<u32>`, `cullBatch(clip)` returning `vec4(0, 0, -1, 1)` when the batch's word is non-zero, wired into both colour-module vertex entry points; `DEPTH_VERTEX` untouched.",
    "why": "A culled batch is dropped by the rasteriser instead of a branch in the fragment stage: one degenerate vertex position and the draw costs nothing, and the object is still visible to the depth-only paths (the prepass is what the HiZ pyramid reduces).",
    "note": "The shadow and depth-only entry points deliberately do not read the buffer: the prepass is the producer of the depth the culler tests against, so a culled batch still has to lay its depth down."
  },

    "summary": "Phase 13.5: the device culls objects. `GpuObjectCuller` (`engine/src/rendering/objectCulling.ts`) takes the frame's batches as one bounds entry each (AABB + the batch's per-object distance limit in `min.w`) and writes one u32 visibility word per batch, which the standard shader's vertex stage reads at `batchVisibility[objectData.visibilityIndex]` and answers by pushing the whole batch below the near plane (`cullBatch` -> `vec4(0,0,-1,1)`; a draw cannot express \"zero instances\" without 13.6's indirect path). Three tests run on the device in one pass: frustum (the six planes from `viewProj`, sphere against plane), distance (per batch, the merged limit), and HiZ occlusion against a four-level max-pyramid the same module builds from `scene.depth` (2x2 reduce, view-space metres, level k = max of its four children, rectangle chosen per level by the batch's screen span, one texel walk; conservatively visible when the near plane straddles the bounds or the pyramid is not there). Counters are `atomic<u32>` and read back one frame late, because that is what the gate found first: Tint has no plain-`u32` `atomicAdd` overload and the mock, `check:wgsl` and 584 tests were all green on a shader no GPU would compile (same class as 13.4's parenthesised shift). The pass order is `forge.prepass` -> `forge.hiz.0..3` -> `forge.objects.cull` -> SSAO, so occlusion tests what the prepass just laid down; the culler keeps `hizLevelsFrame` apart from `hizLevels` so a frame with no prepass cannot make a pass read a texture nothing wrote (the render graph's own rule, previously a `UsageError`). `RendererOptions.objectCulling = auto|cpu|gpu` and `occlusionCulling`, plus `RenderStats.cullTested/cullFrustum/cullDistance/cullOccluded` and the demo's `?objectculling=`/`?occlusionculling=` and HUD line drive it; the CPU twin `cullBatchesOnCpu`/`buildHizOnCpu` is what the mock device runs, so every existing CPU gate sees real verdicts, and `Renderable.maxDistance` is the new per-object knob. The second real-device-only bug was the HiZ rectangle's y: NDC +y is up and texel row 0 is the top, so the mirrored rectangle proved floating geometry occluded against rows nearer than it \u2014 the gate saw it as `16161 px differ by up to 162.0 luma levels` in the prepass A/B, and the fix (`pixel.y = (0.5 - ndc.y * 0.5) * extent.y`, the same shape in the twin) is pinned by a floor-depth test that fails if the twin's sign is flipped. Measured: `tests/objectCulling.test.ts` 16 tests (mirrors, pyramid sizing/metres/limit, frustum + distance + occlusion sweeps, `MAX_CULLED_BATCHES`, the two-frame level count), `tests/frame.test.ts` 24 (default is `cpu` with zeroed words and `cullTested === batches`; the sky camera's batch is `CullReason.Frustum`; the gpu arm adds `forge.objects.cull` + `forge.hiz.0` and dispatches ceil(batches/64); a cpu->gpu round trip re-adds the pass rather than reusing a disposed culler), 42 suites / 584 tests, and the real-device gate: gpu vs cpu over the fixture 5 batches / 5 tested / max luma diff 0.00 / 0 px beyond one level, `forge.objects.cull` owned by the gpu arm and absent from the cpu arm, occlusion on->off 4 HiZ passes -> 0 with 0 px darker and 0 px beyond one level, restored to `mode gpu, occlusion true` -- and no new GPU errors. benchmarks/src/culling.bench.ts (in `npm run bench`) measures the twin at 0.892 us/batch over 2048 batches and 1.118 us at 8192 (1.25x for 4x the batches); the 8192 cap costs 9.16 ms/frame (3.01 frustum, 3.70 with the distance limits), and the 1280x720 four-level pyramid 39.52 ms/frame -- the reduction the twin does not do and the reason the device is the default. Docs: `docs/RENDERING.md` section 4d (the one-word contract, the twin, the pass order, the atomics and their one-frame lag, the 13.6 boundary), `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md` (13.5 closed; two follow-ups opened: per-instance culling and cascade culling through the same pass), `docs/VERIFICATION.md` (including the note that the Mars HGA poll is environment-bound here). Capabilities: `rendering.gpuCulling` verified, `rendering.cullCoverage` partial (closes 13.6's per-batch boundary, the 8192 cap, the twin has no occlusion, uploads still happen), `rendering.depthReuse` now names its three consumers. `npm run verify`, `lint:arch`, `check:testmap`, `tsc -p benchmarks` and `docs:check` are green (92 capabilities: 47 verified / 25 partial / 16 planned / 4 deferred).     "what": "The cull pass now writes the frame's draw commands and the visible-batch list alongside the visibility word. `ObjectBatchEntry.max.w` carries the batch's instance count, `ObjectCullStatsBlock` grew to six `atomic<u32>` (`visible`, `recordZeroed`), and the shader gained bindings 5 `drawRecords: array<u32>` and 6 `visibleBatches: array<u32>` plus the constants `CULL_FLAG_RECORDS`, `DRAW_RECORD_WORDS` 8 / `DRAW_RECORD_BYTES` 32 / `DRAW_RECORD_INSTANCES` 1. The verdict is computed once (`cullReasonOf`, extracted so the text pins the algebra the twin mirrors) and one write site turns it into the word, the counter, `slot = atomicAdd(&counts.visible, 1u)` into the list and word 1 of the batch's record: the batch's own count when visible, 0 plus `recordZeroed` when not.     "summary": "Phase 13.6: indirect rendering. The cull pass no longer stops at a verdict \u2014 it writes the frame's draw commands. One 32-byte record per batch (`DRAW_RECORD_WORDS` 8, `DRAW_RECORD_BYTES` 32, `DRAW_RECORD_INSTANCES` 1, 16-aligned slots so `drawIndexedIndirect` and `drawIndirect` both read them) lives in `cull.drawRecords` (`STORAGE | INDIRECT | COPY_DST`, grown in 256-byte steps): the CPU seeds the index window from the batch (indexCount / count / indexStart, 0 for a non-indexed batch) and the pass owns **word 1 alone** \u2014 the batch's instance count (uploaded as `ObjectBatchEntry.max.w`) when the verdict is visible, `0` plus `recordZeroed` when it is not. The verdict is computed once (`cullReasonOf`, extracted), and one write site turns it into the visibility word, the counter, `slot = atomicAdd(&counts.visible, 1u)` into `cull.visibleBatches` (the compacted list of survivors, at most `MAX_CULLED_BATCHES`, in the device's own order) and the record, so nothing in the frame can disagree with what the vertex stage read. The twin writes exactly the same words (`cullBatchesOnCpu` with `ObjectCullOutputs`, behind `CULL_FLAG_RECORDS`), and the pass only touches `index < min(batchCount, MAX_CULLED_BATCHES)` \u2014 the renderer pre-fills every slot with the batch's own count, so a slot past the cap keeps saying \"draw\". `Renderer.indirectDraws` (default on, `invalidate()` on change) submits `forge.main` through `drawIndexedIndirect` / `drawIndirect` at `batch.cullIndex * DRAW_RECORD_BYTES`; the direct arm is kept as the A/B \u2014 same batches, same words, same pixels \u2014 and sets no `CULL_FLAG_RECORDS`, so it pays for no record it will not read. Shadow and prepass keep their own draws and their own culling. `RenderStats` gained `cullVisible`, `cullRecordZeroed` and `indirectDraws` (the first two through the same one-frame-late readback as 13.5's counters). The mock device now parses the record out of `buffer.data` for both indirect draws and logs its fields, which is the only reason a CPU gate can assert the device-side instance count: `tests/objectCulling.test.ts` (19, was 16) pins the shader's single write site, the twin's outputs and both identities (`visible = tested - culled`, `recordZeroed = sum(culled)`), and \u2014 with sentinel-filled buffers \u2014 that a frame without the flag writes nothing and that past the cap the CPU's count survives; `tests/frame.test.ts` (27, was 24) asserts the records drive the frame, that the two submission paths differ by exactly the culled batches' `indexCount * instanceCount` vertices (read out of `draw.uniforms`, on a fixture whose 1 m draw distance makes the device, not the CPU, the decider), and that the flag follows the switch. `npm run verify` (42 files / 590 tests + check:wgsl), `lint:arch`, `check:testmap` and `docs:check` (92 capabilities: 48 verified / 25 partial / 15 planned / 4 deferred) are green. `check:browser` gained the arm that only a device can settle: a 1 m draw distance over the fixture makes the device drop batches the frame built, the two submission paths then have to draw the same picture to the pixel (one through a zero-instance record, one through 13.5's collapsed clip position), the direct arm must issue zero indirect draws and the same number of draw calls, and the pass's counters must satisfy `recordZeroed = culled` on the record arm and `0` on the direct one. It **did not run locally** \u2014 the sandbox snapshot has no browser (`~/.cache` is excluded and the Playwright CDN is unreachable), so the gate exits 2 with `NOT RUN \u2014 no launchable browser`, which `docs/VERIFICATION.md` now documents as its own state \u2014 but the PR's advisory WebGPU job ran it on a real SwiftShader adapter and passed end to end: `check:browser passed (real WebGPU, headless Chromium + SwiftShader) \u2014 gpu: adapter ok (google / swiftshader)`, the Phase 13.6 arm included, ~17 minutes after the push.",

    "id": "0350",
    "date": "2026-10-05T16:35:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a10a15-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/renderer.ts",
    "what": "Both population writeBuffer calls now upload an exactly-sized data.subarray(0, count * (INSTANCE_STRIDE >> 2)) view and never pass a size argument (with a spec-citation comment).",
    "why": "14.3 bug: writeBuffer's size/dataOffset are counted in *elements* for TypedArray sources per the W3C spec (Chromium 153 confirmed by probe), so the byte counts (2880/1280) produced 4x oversize writes (11520 B into a 2880 B buffer) that failed on real WebGPU while the mock accepted them."
  },
  {
    "id": "0351",
    "date": "2026-10-05T16:35:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a10a15-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/testing/mockGpu.ts",
    "what": "Mock writeBuffer now implements the spec's element-count semantics: element size from the source's BYTES_PER_ELEMENT (DataView = 1), integer-range checks, start = dataOffset * elementBytes, write size = size * elementBytes or the remaining view.",
    "why": "The mock's stale byte semantics accepted oversized writes that real devices reject \u2014 that is why every unit suite passed while the real-WebGPU population renders failed; the mock is the foundation the mock-GPU suites assert against."
  },
  {
    "id": "0352",
    "date": "2026-10-05T16:35:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a10a15-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/scene/population.ts",
    "what": "PopulationInstanceBlock gains a monotonic revision counter and markModified().",
    "why": "The device-resident buffer (14.3) must re-upload exactly when content changed; scatter and remesh re-anchoring are the only mutators, so a revision bump is the complete signal."
  },
  {
    "id": "0353",
    "date": "2026-10-05T16:35:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a10a15-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/population/scatter.ts",
    "what": "scatterPopulationChunk marks the block modified on every path that can write instances (including the early-return empty/cap paths).",
    "why": "A revision that misses a content change would leave a stale device buffer; the early paths reset the live prefix and must move the revision too."
  },
  {
    "id": "0354",
    "date": "2026-10-05T16:35:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": null,
    "branch": "arena/01a10a15-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/population/world.ts",
    "what": "The remesh Y re-anchor calls block.markModified() (and skips zero-count blocks).",
    "why": "Re-anchoring moves the positions, so the device-resident buffer must re-upload; without the bump the old matrix would stay resident."
  },
  {
    "id": "0355",
    "date": "2026-10-05T16:35:00Z",
    "type": "change",

    "why": "14.3's contract is 'upload once, copy never' \u2014 without these assertions the per-frame-copy regression the issue describes would be invisible to the suite."

    "why": "The LOD entries need the window boundary per draw and the compute pass needs one 32-byte record per dispatch; the pad slot was always per-batch headroom, and 14.4 gives it a purpose without changing the layout (still 176 B, check:wgsl-verified)."

    "file": "engine/src/resources/streaming.ts",
    "what": "New: AssetStreamer \u2014 request() queues, pump() admits highest-priority-first under a maxConcurrent cap and a per-frame uploadBudgetBytes (charged by descriptor.estimatedBytes), newFrame() resets the budget, cancel(id) drops queued loads outright and aborts in-flight ones via the registry, settle() simulates frames until drained, dispose() rejects queued loads. Holds one registry handle per in-flight load (released before the caller's continuation runs) so in-flight entries are eviction-safe and settled entries are evictable.",
    "why": "Phase 15.3: large scenes must load assets incrementally without blocking the simulation loop \u2014 the registry loads-on-acquire shape cannot prioritize, cap or budget."
  },

    "id": "0410",

    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/resources/registry.ts",
    "what": "ResourceDescriptor gains estimatedBytes (pre-load upload estimate for the streamer's budget); new cancelLoad(id) sets the in-flight entry's abort flag (output disposed, entry fails with a cancellation error, next acquire retries); startLoad now gives every attempt a fresh abort signal (previously a cancelLoad'd retry inherited aborted=true and discarded its own output \u2014 a pre-existing latent bug the acquire-retry path could hit; retry()'s manual reset is now redundant and removed). Header rules 5-7 document the 15.x additions.",
    "why": "Cancellation is a first-class registry operation the streamer drives; the abort-signal fix makes cancel-then-reload actually work."

    "what": "Solve the wheel slip on the demand's own face: bracket Newton to [min(0, side*peakSlip), max(0, side*peakSlip)] with a bisection fallback; treat only positive drive torque as traction-controlled (regen is negative drive); add a stepWheelSpeed hold guard so a brake that out-torques the drive keeps the wheel at zero; replace parallel steering with applySteering(), an Ackermann turn centre (unsteered axle as the pivot line, commanded lock on the inner wheel).",
    "why": "The brake demand could leave the tire's peak on the falling flank and clamp to the mirrored slip limit, so a pinned brake delivered peak forward force and the rover ran away downhill (43-49 m/s in 3 s); regen behind a pad torque wound a locked wheel backwards to -2500 rad/s; and parallel steer put the corner wheels at their own slip angles, whose lateral answer ate the rover's whole traction budget (throttle + steer crawled at 0.133 m/s)."

    "id": "0602",
    "date": "2026-10-07T02:50:00Z",
    "type": "pr-merge",
    "pr": 64,
    "branch": "arena/f0d99231-forge-engine",
    "base": "main",
    "title": "Fix the rover's slope-brake runaway and steering stall; raise its speed 50%",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "summary": "Three independent rover defects fixed, plus the requested +50% speed. (1) Braking on a slope drove the rover faster: `balanceLongitudinal` solved the wheel slip with a cross-zero Newton step clamped to \u00b1peakSlip, so a full-brake demand the tire cannot deliver walked off the Pacejka peak, overshot and settled on the mirrored clamp \u2014 peak forward force with the brake pinned (25 deg descent, 6.95 m/s -> ~49 m/s in 3 s, kappa pinned at +0.285). The solve now brackets the demand's own face ([min(0, side*peakSlip), max(0, side*peakSlip)]), Newton with a bisection fallback; regenerative braking (negative drive torque) no longer counts as traction-controlled, and `stepWheelSpeed` holds a wheel whose brake out-torques the drive instead of winding it backwards past zero. (2) Throttle + steering stalled the rover: every steered wheel took the same angle, so the corner wheels sat off their own turn circles and their lateral tire force acted as drag on a ~1 kW drivetrain \u2014 full throttle + full lock crawled at 0.133 m/s, which is also why the obstacle course read as not moving. New `applySteering` builds one Ackermann turn centre (commanded lock on the inner wheel, unsteered axle as the pivot line); full lock under full throttle now reaches 1.88 m/s, and the real course W+D run holds >2 m/s. (3) Speed: the requested +50% scales the speed axis, not the power boost PR #62 rejected \u2014 torque stays 9.5 N.m, base speed 1000->1500 rpm, power cap 1000->1500 W (continuous at the base speed), no-load 3800->5700 rpm (2.63 m/s). Measured loaded speeds 1.574 -> 2.361 m/s on the course and 1.625 -> 2.438 m/s on Mars regolith, exactly 1.500x, with an unchanged launch. Validation: npm run verify passed 819 tests in 57 suites (typecheck + WGSL), lint:arch/check:testmap/docs:check green, CPU CI passed, and the real-WebGPU gate passed on this box (dz=0.52 m at maxSpeed=1.13 m/s in 0.92 s of throttle over 11 presented frames, contact=6, HGA az=168.0, arm stowed, zero GPU errors).",

    "what": "Before `npm ci`, fetch the @sparticuz/chromium tarball with `curl` (not npm's fetcher) and seed npm's cache \u2014 content plus index entry, through the cacache bundled inside npm itself \u2014 so `npm ci` serves it from cache. The URL and the sha512 the download is verified against come from package-lock.json; a present tarball is reused only when its sha512 matches. Every failure degrades to 'let npm fetch it itself'. Moved TMP up so the step-4 seed and the step-5 browser share it.",
    "why": "In sandboxed egress environments npm's fetcher aborts the ~70 MB chromium download with ERR_SSL_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED while a plain curl of the same registry URL completes, so `npm ci` (and thus the whole setup) failed before any test could run. Seeding the cache from a curl-fetched, hash-verified tarball keeps the lockfile authoritative (still `npm ci`, never `npm install`) while removing the one fetch that cannot succeed."

(2) The mock now dispatches uncapturederror as the { error } event a real GPUDevice does (listeners read event.error) and gains reportUncapturedError() for tests. (3) setup-deps.sh fetches the @sparticuz/chromium tarball with curl \u2014 npm's fetcher aborts the ~70 MB download in sandboxed egress with ERR_SSL_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED \u2014 verifies its sha512 against package-lock.json, and seeds the verified bytes into npm's cache so npm ci stays authoritative and succeeds.     "summary": "ROADMAP Phase 16.6 is complete; Phase 16 now remains open only for `assets.gltfAdvanced` (16.1). (1) Rig - engine/src/animation/mechanical.ts: `MechanicalRig` binds one entity per joint to a named channel and poses it as `base \u2218 motion` recomposed from the authored TRS every frame, so re-posing is idempotent (no drift): `revolute` (angle about a parent-frame axis), `prismatic` (offset along it) and `aim` (solved so the joint's local direction points at a target entity, with `stretch` scaling the link to the target distance so a damper reaches its hub). `min`/`max` clamps, `slew` rate limits in units/s, `wrap` for odometers, allocation-free module scratch, and aim solves against the *live local store* rather than the cached world matrices (band 500 writes those later), so a joint declared after the ones it watches sees their pose from the same frame. `valueOf(channel)` / `saturatedChannel(channel)` read the posed value back after ratio/bias/clamp/slew - what a HUD or a gate must compare pixels against, not the raw channel. (2) System - animation/mechanicalSystem.ts: `MechanicalChannelSource` writes a frame's channels, then `MechanicalSystem` (order 310, after AnimationSystem and after the fixed simulation band that produces the inputs) advances (limits + slew) and poses per `MechanicalRigComponent`; stats mechanicalRigs / mechanicalJoints / ...Posed / ...Solved / ...Saturated. (3) Vehicles - vehicles/wheelRig.ts: `createVehicleWheelRig` binds wheel telemetry to joints in solve order (hub-carrier travel, the wheel's *own* Ackermann angle - so the rear knuckles the solver left at zero stay at zero - the odometer axle with its ratio sign-flipped on the left so both sides roll forward, then arm and damper aims), and `VehicleWheelSource` feeds them. The Phase 6 playground drops its per-corner boxes for real assemblies (tyre, rim, 14 cleats, 8 wheel-nuts, upright, trailing arm, damper) and gains a `setWheelOverride` gate hook plus posed-value telemetry. (4) Second consumer - the Mars rover's five-joint GLB arm is posed by a rig from the controller's channels instead of a hand-written loop (`wrap: false` is load-bearing: the unfold deliberately takes the elbow the long way round at -242 degrees, and wrapping into (-pi, pi] would flip it through the ground), and `marsState().armPivotDeg` reads the angles back off the transform store.     "what": "New demo-side river module: bounded-curvature meander path integrated into a station table, a cross-section elevation field (thalweg, point bar, cut bank, levee, back-swamp) resolved as the minimum over every channel branch that reaches a point, plus a tributary igarape, four oxbow lakes, journey marks and a channel-following ribbon builder for terrain and the water sheet.",
    "why": "The Amazon boat demo needs one height field that the terrain mesh, the boat's grounding query and the jungle scatter all agree on. Engine terrain stages cannot carve an authored navigable path (ValleyCarvingGenerator is flow-accumulation driven), and composing features as a min of absolute profiles leaves dry channels and creases, so the floodplain is authored as deltas on one shared upland base."
  },

    "date": "2026-10-11T13:38:27Z",

    "what": "Waterplane-column hull model for the launch: the lofting function is the single source of flotation geometry, each column carries a buoyancy force integrated from a per-column volume table, with heave damping measured against the wave's own vertical motion, planing lift, a wave-making drag hump near Froude 0.42, current-relative flow, prop-wash steering and keel grounding against the bed. Work in progress: statics verified, drag and lift coefficients not yet tuned, no scene imports it.",
    "why": "Keeping the boat outside engine/src avoids production @covers claims (repo precedent: examples/src/scenes/alpineSnowpack.ts), and deriving draft, trim, gm and roll period by solving the lofted shape means the visual hull and the floating hull cannot drift apart."

    "branch": "arena/51731dcd-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "examples/src/scenes/amazonBoatSim.ts",
    "what": "Retuned and repaired the launch's dynamics: the per-column water push is now rotated into body axes before it is accumulated, thrust is a longitudinal force applied at the leg (its lever and its trim-driven vertical component replace the ad-hoc bow-down couple), planing lift now acts at the centroid of the *wetted* columns so the trim is self-limiting, the rocker and leg tilt are angle-of-attack offsets rather than separate forces, the propeller loses its grip with the outboard leg trimmed out and with the bottom out of contact, the outboard leg's interference drag and the crossflow grip are sized with water density and the correct sign, heave and lift are bounded by the displacement, pitch gets its own damping, and floatation is solved by a bisection over draft and trim using the step's own force law. Mass 1450 to 1260 kg; new exports riverChop, legDragArea/legDragDown/legDragClear, legTrimAngle and pitchDamping replace liftCoefficient/rockerLift-only tuning; new state field legTrim drives thrust, trim, yaw damping and drag.",
    "why": "WOT sat near 2 m/s and any chop produced NaN inside a few seconds. The causes were frame and axis errors, not coefficients: a world vector added to a body-frame accumulator, thrust on the transverse axis, and a rocker term that reached 41 kN against a 14.2 kN displacement. With those out, the hull-speed wall is crossed by rising on her own lift, which is the behaviour the model is supposed to demonstrate."
  },

    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "summary": "Two demo-side modules for the Amazon river boat demo, with the hull tuned and pinned by tests. `examples/src/scenes/amazonRiver.ts` authors the floodplain as one height field: a bounded-curvature meander path integrated into a station table (|dtheta/ds| <= 0.0023 so a nearest-station query stays unique inside the channel's influence band), a cross-section profile (thalweg, point bar, cut bank, levee, back swamp) resolved as the minimum over every channel branch that reaches a point, an igarape tributary, four oxbow lakes, journey marks, and a ribbon builder that turns the field into the terrain mesh and the water sheet (4200 m journey, 295 ms terrain build, 3 us per elevation query, 0 dry stations, max drawn edge slope 0.87). `examples/src/scenes/amazonBoatSim.ts` is a waterplane-column hull for a 9.4 m / 1260 kg launch: the lofting function `hullHalfWidth(t, h)` is the only source of flotation geometry, each column carries buoyancy and waterplane-width tables integrated from it, and the design floatation (draft 0.353 m, trim, GM 3.16 m, roll period 1.38 s) is *solved* by bisecting draft and trim against the same force law the integrator uses, so panel loads sum to the displacement weight within 1 N and the settle agrees with the solve to 1.5 mm and 0.01 degrees. Forces: skin friction over the wetted surface with a wave-making hump at Froude 0.42 (the hull-speed wall), planing lift on the *wetted* columns acting at their own centroid so the trim limits itself, heave damping against the water's own vertical motion, slam, current-relative flow, prop-wash steering, outboard leg trim as a control, and grounding against the bed. `riverChop` is the shared wind-sea field: four Gerstner trains, none under 16 m, all under the breaking limit, fanned across the wind. Measured: 15.1 m/s at WOT holding steady on flat water, a 4.3/9.0/11.9/15.1 throttle ladder, leg trim worth 3.2 m/s, a bounded 60 s soak in a 1.3 m quartering sea (8.7 degrees max roll, 0.35 m least freeboard, no NaN), a bar shoaling 11 cm/m grounds her and backing off works in 14 s, and 30 Hz matches 240 Hz to 0.4 m/s. `tests/examples/amazonBoatHull.test.ts` (15 cases) pins all of it, linked in `tests/full.test.ts` (73 suites), with `tests/tools/selrun.test.ts`, `docs/TESTING.md` and `docs/VERIFICATION.md` carrying the new suite and case counts (1 064 cases, 654 coverage claims); `mnemosyne.md` records the four dynamics bugs (world-versus-body force frame, thrust on the transverse axis, a static solve that was not the runtime's force law, and rocker double-counted as a lift force) and that `findBankSite` returning null on a cut bank is correct behaviour.     "id": "1214",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/environment/multiScattering.ts",
    "what": "New: the Phase 17.1 reference implementation of multiple scattering \u2014 `MultiScatteringConfig`, `MULTI_SCATTERING_CPU` (16x16 table, 32 directions, 12 steps, a 24x32 tau table) and `MULTI_SCATTERING_GPU` (32x32, 48 directions, 24 steps), the sqrt-height and terminator-centred sun warps with their inverses, and `MultiScatteringField` (build, bilinear `sample`, `texelValue`, `meanRatio`, per-channel `seriesRatio`, `totalScattering`, `texelIndex`, allocation-free scratch), plus `transposeMultiScatteringTable`.",
    "why": "Single scattering makes the sky ~3x darker than reality, keeps the twilight telescope-sharp and reads yellow at an Earth horizon; the light it misses is what the higher orders carry. Compiled the standard isotropic-source geometric-series approximation (J1 = the sphere mean of the model's own single scattering, L_ms = J1 / (1 - rho)) into one (height, sun elevation) table, so a reader needs one lookup per sample instead of a nested quadrature."
  },
  {
    "id": "1215",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/environment/atmosphere.ts",
    "what": "Added `ESTIMATE_MIE_ANISOTROPY` (0.5) and exported `clampMieAnisotropy` (`clampG` is now an alias); `skyAmbient`/`horizonColor` call the exported one. `AtmosphereModel` gained the `multiScattering: MultiScatteringField | null` member, and `skyRadiance` adds its term per march step.",
    "why": "A forward-peaked Mie lobe cannot be averaged by a few dozen directions \u2014 whichever sample lands nearest the sun dominates. Measured on Mars dust (g 0.7) the 32/48-direction mean came out 1.5-2x too bright, and texels near the terminator spiked by an order of magnitude. Capping the lobe at 0.5 keeps the scattered energy while redistributing it to what the sample set can resolve; it is the same cap the ambient estimate already used, now one shared constant in both the CPU and GPU paths."
  },
  {
    "id": "1216",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/environment/index.ts",
    "what": "Re-export `multiScattering.js` and list the module in the folder's header comment.",
    "why": "Keep the environment barrel complete: the field and its configs are part of the environment API."
  },
  {
    "id": "1217",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/shaders/multiScattering.ts",
    "what": "New: the GPU twin of the table. `WGSL_ATMOSPHERE_COMMON` bakes the named `MS_*` constants from the TS config and carries the shared phase functions and `msOpticalDepthToSpace`; `csTransmittance` fills the tau table (blocked rays store `MS_BLOCKED_TAU`) and `csField` the LUT (Fibonacci directions, cubic view march, the same warped axes). `MS_BINDINGS` (2 = table, 3 = LUT), `MS_WORKGROUP` 64, `MS_ENTRY`, the texel-count constants and `wgslMultiScatteringSampler` round it out.",
    "why": "The table has to exist on the device for the sky pass to read it, built by two dispatches that share one bind-group layout (deliberately not the sky pass's LUT binding, so a shader cannot hard-code an index that only works in one of the two programs). Every WGSL resolution and count is generated from the TS config, so a retune cannot desynchronise the twins."
  },
  {
    "id": "1218",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/skyMultiScattering.ts",
    "what": "New: `GpuMultiScattering` \u2014 the table and LUT storage buffers (the LUT is STORAGE | COPY_DST | COPY_SRC), the table/field compute pipelines, `record` (the `forge.sky.ms.table` and `forge.sky.ms.lut` passes), `prepare` (lazily creates and returns the LUT buffer the sky pass binds), `readLut()` (staging buffer + `mapAsync`, `unmap`/`destroy` in a `finally`), `dispose`, plus `MS_SUN_EPSILON` and the 22-float effective-atmosphere signature helpers.",
    "why": "Owns the device-side table and, through `readLut`, makes it observable \u2014 the numeric half of the Phase 17.1 acceptance is the device's table compared with a CPU twin of the same frame, which needs a staging readback. The signature comparison lets a frame skip both passes when neither the atmosphere nor the sun changed, so a steady frame's work is unchanged from before this phase."
  },
  {
    "id": "1219",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/shaders/common.ts",
    "what": "Added and expanded the shared atmosphere WGSL block: `WGSL_ATMOSPHERE_FUNCTIONS` (ray/sphere roots, the ozone tent, Rayleigh and Cornette-Shanks phase functions, transmittance to space), used by the sky pass and both compute passes.",
    "why": "One definition of the atmosphere in WGSL instead of one per module: the sky pass and the two table passes must march the same atmosphere, and the CPU twin (`atmosphere.ts`) already had the single copy the GPU side was missing."
  },
  {
    "id": "1220",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/shaders/sky.ts",
    "what": "The sky pass gained the multiple-scattering term: it reads the LUT at `SKY_BINDINGS.multiScattering`, looks the warped table up per march step, and adds `T_view * (sigma_R * rho_R + sigma_M * rho_M) * J_ms` gated on `sky.multiScattering`.",
    "why": "This is the payoff for the phase: every sky pixel gains the higher orders inside the march that already tracks transmittance, at one table lookup per sample, instead of being a sky that is simply too dark with a yellow horizon."
  },
  {
    "id": "1221",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/renderer.ts",
    "what": "Wired 17.1 into the frame: `recordSkyMultiScattering` (recorded before the shadow cascades, rebuilding only for a fresh renderer, a sun past `MS_SUN_EPSILON` or a changed effective atmosphere), `ensureSkyMultiScatteringLut` plus the sky bind group's LUT entry, `readMultiScatteringLut()`, `multiScatteringReference()` (the CPU twin of the last sky frame's effective atmosphere under the GPU config), the monotonic `multiScatteringBuilds` counter, `SkyUniforms.multiScattering` in `writeSky`/`resolveSky`, and disposal.",
    "why": "The renderer is where the table meets the frame: the two dispatches must run before anything samples the LUT, must be skipped when nothing changed, and must be readable so the device's numbers can be checked against the reference implementation on the same frame. The counter exists because a conditional pass is otherwise only observable through timings or pixels."
  },
  {
    "id": "1222",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/pipeline.ts",
    "what": "The sky bind-group layout gained its fourth entry: `SKY_BINDINGS.multiScattering` as a fragment-visible read-only storage buffer.",
    "why": "The sky pass reads the table the compute pass writes. It stays bound whether or not the term is enabled, so toggling `sky.multiScattering` never re-creates a bind group mid-frame."
  },
  {
    "id": "1223",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/uniforms.ts",
    "what": "`SkyUniforms` gained `multiScattering` (i32, offset 120), which moves `viewSamples` to 124 and the struct to 144 bytes.",
    "why": "The sky pass needs the flag the scene sets. The struct is generated, so the offset shift is mechanical \u2014 and the WGSL layout checks pin it."
  },
  {
    "id": "1224",
    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/scene/scene.ts",
    "what": "`SceneSkySettings` gained `multiScattering` (default `true`), serialised and validated like its neighbours in `applySettings`.",
    "why": "The feature belongs to the scene's sky settings, not to renderer options: it is a look/perf decision a scene can make, and it has to survive `serialize()` -> `applySerialized()` with the rest of the sky block."
  },
  {

    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",

    "date": "2026-10-11T23:58:00Z",

    "id": "1242",
    "date": "2026-10-12T04:20:00Z",
    "type": "pr-merge",
    "pr": 81,
    "branch": "arena/d1891e90-forge-engine",
    "base": "main",
    "title": "Phase 17.1: multiple scattering (table, two compute passes, both twins)",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "summary": "Phase 17.1 of the roadmap: the sky gains the second-and-higher scattering orders. `environment/multiScattering.ts` is the CPU reference \u2014 the isotropic-source geometric series (J1 = the sphere mean of the model's own single scattering, L_ms = J1 / (1 - rho)) precomputed into a (height, sun elevation) table with a sqrt-height and a terminator-centred sqrt(|mu|) sun warp, at two resolutions (CPU 16x16/32 directions/12 steps, GPU 32x32/48 directions/24 steps). `rendering/shaders/multiScattering.ts` and `rendering/skyMultiScattering.ts` are the device twin: `forge.sky.ms.table` and `forge.sky.ms.lut` compute passes recorded ahead of the frame and only when a fresh renderer, a sun past MS_SUN_EPSILON or a changed effective atmosphere needs them, with a staging readback (`readLut`) for verification. The sky pass adds T_view*(sigma_R*rho_R + sigma_M*rho_M)*J_ms per march step, gated on `scene.settings.sky.multiScattering` (default on; SkyUniforms 128 -> 144 B, the LUT as the sky layout's fourth binding). Both twins clamp the Mie lobe at ESTIMATE_MIE_ANISOTROPY (0.5): without it a 48-direction mean of Mars' dust (g 0.7) is decided by whichever sample lands nearest the sun and comes out 1.5-2x too bright. Measured against a 256-direction reference the device table is within ~7 % in daylight below 25 km and the CPU one within ~20 %, both exactly zero below each row's horizon, with the terminator columns good to a factor of ~2 (documented, not chased \u2014 the source changes by orders of magnitude inside one column). Rendered gains on the CPU configuration: Earth x1.26 zenith / x1.30 horizon away from the sun / x2.2 zenith 6 deg after sunset / x6.3 at that hour's horizon, Mars x2.2-4.95. Cost: CPU build ~9 ms; on SwiftShader the device's own timestamps measured 0.11 ms + 43.43 ms on rebuild frames and nothing on the frames that skip it. Verification: `tests/environment/environment17.test.ts` (22 cases), the frame/wgsl/selrun count updates, `npm run verify` (1,086 cases in 74 suites), and `npm run check:browser:environment` on real Chromium + SwiftShader \u2014 the table rebuilt exactly once per sun step and never on a still frame, the table read back off the adapter matching the CPU twin of the same frame within 0.01 % at twelve daylight texels with exactly zero nadir columns, and switching the term off darkening 156,062 of 468,000 pixels (max 10 luma levels) while brightening none.",

    "file": "examples/src/scenes/weatherScene.ts",
    "what": "`triggerLightning` registers the strike first and resumes the audio context alongside it (`void audio.resume().catch(...)`), instead of chaining the strike behind `audio.resume().then(...)`.",
    "why": "The advisory browser gate failed on CI with `triggered lightning did not register a strike` (strikes=0). Root cause is not the scheduler: the strike was chained behind `AudioSystem.resume()`, and under the headless autoplay policy with no gesture yet `context.resume()` never settles, so the promise never ran `lightning.trigger()`. The demo's own thunder callback already gates on `context.state === \"running\"`, so nothing is lost by letting the strike and the audio resume race: a tap on Strike now always registers a strike, and the thunder follows when the browser lets the context run. Re-run locally: `weather lightning: strikes=2`."
  },

Both are now the checks they were meant to be, and the loader poll's label states what it can and cannot see."

    "file": "engine/src/gpu/shaderCache.ts",
    "what": "`validateWgsl` gains `derivativeControlFlowIssues`: it rejects `dpdx`/`dpdy`/`fwidth` reached through a branch (`if`/`else`/`for`/`while`/`switch`/`loop`) on non-uniform-looking data.",

    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",

    "file": "engine/src/rendering/pipeline.ts",
    "what": "The frame-layout entry for `BINDINGS.cloud` (fragment-visible uniform, `minBindingSize` = `CloudUniforms.byteSize`) is now written out explicitly in the frame bind group layout.",
    "why": "A bind group layout has no optional slots: the surface shaders read the deck's shadow block, so every frame that compiles a surface pipeline has to declare it."
  },
  {
    "id": "1252",
    "date": "2026-10-12T16:46:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 83,
    "branch": "arena/98a1a21d-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/renderer.ts",
    "what": "`writeClouds` packs the sub-layer records into a reused `Float32Array(MAX_CLOUD_LAYERS * 4)` scratch \u2014 `(driftX, driftZ, centre, weight)` per sheet, the drift evaluated at the frame clock \u2014 and writes the new art fields plus the shadow fields into the cloud block.",
    "why": "The CPU owns the layer geometry, so the shader cannot re-derive a height or a weight it could disagree with; the scratch keeps the per-frame path allocation-free, and the drift is metres at the frame's own clock rather than a second time base."
  },
  {
    "id": "1253",
    "date": "2026-10-12T16:46:00Z",

    "why": "The block is the only channel between the CPU's layer geometry and the shader's sampling of it; it had to describe the stack before anything could draw it."

  {

    "why": "These are art-direction knobs, so they belong to the scene (serialized with it) rather than to the weather drive \u2014 and `layers = 1` is the Phase 8b look, which keeps the setting honest."
  },
  {
    "id": "1255",
    "date": "2026-10-12T16:46:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 83,
    "branch": "arena/98a1a21d-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/shaders/cloudLayer.ts",
    "what": "`WGSL_CLOUD` became the stack's GPU twin: it samples every sub-layer record, weights the column, marches the sun ray through the slab above each sample for the self-shadow, and fades octaves whose wavelength is under the pixel's footprint (the footprint passed in from the caller, since derivatives are legal only in uniform control flow).",
    "why": "This is where the shimmer and the flat shading were actually fixed; the CPU side defines the formulas and this file is their device implementation, kept line-for-line comparable on purpose."
  },
  {
    "id": "1256",
    "date": "2026-10-12T16:46:00Z",
    "type": "change",
    "pr": 83,
    "branch": "arena/98a1a21d-forge-engine",
    "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "file": "engine/src/rendering/shaders/sky.ts",
    "what": "The sky pass takes the deck's sampling footprint as its first statement and passes it to `cloudDeck`.",
    "why": "The derivative has to be taken by a fullscreen-triangle pixel before any ground/sky branch, or WebKit and Tint both reject the module; taking it once also removes a per-sample derivative."
  },

  "what": "New diag module: five bisect variants of the live `sky.wgsl` (loop bounds without the per-pixel `select`, compile-time bounds, no multiple-scattering storage read, no cloud-deck mix, fragment stage short-circuited to a constant), cut from the shipped source by anchored line surgery that returns null when an anchor moves.",
  "why": "iPhone Safari 26.6 shades the sky pure black while every backend in the sandbox renders it and every stat stays green; with no WebKit build here, the candidate fixes have to run on the device, and a variant that silently fails to mutate would measure the wrong thing."

  "why": "The phone report that named the black sky could show the pass running but not whether the driver had compiled the module or which construct zeroed the radiance; the matrix and the failure counter are the two readings that separate those faults."

    "id": "1727",
    "date": "2026-10-17T15:40:00Z",
    "type": "pr-merge",
    "pr": 122,
    "branch": "claude/phase19-snapshots",
    "base": "main",
    "title": "Phase 19.3: exact mid-run simulation snapshots (physics, vehicles, weather, RNG) with state hashing",
    "model": "Claude Opus 5.5",
    "modelVersion": null,
    "summary": "core/snapshot.ts adds structural captureState/restoreState (exact through JSON: tagged -0/NaN/infinities, typed arrays) and hashState (FNV-1a of canonical JSON). PhysicsWorld, Vehicle and Rng gain snapshot/restoreSnapshot (Rng now carries the cached Gaussian and restore() clears it); weather, day/night and the lightning schedule implement SceneObject.snapshotState; systems and components get snapshot hooks. scene/snapshot.ts combines them with transforms, scene settings and the world surface grip into captureSceneSnapshot/restoreSceneSnapshot/hashSceneSnapshot, checking structure before restoring. simulationSnapshot (10 cases) pins that a restored session reaches the uninterrupted run's state hash.   "why": "The profiler was a fixed-position <pre> that could only be shown or hidden: on a phone it buried the scene, it could not be resized to read more rows, and it could not be moved out of the way of the controls you were profiling."
},
{

  "why": "A host that mirrors a panel's state elsewhere - the demo toolbar's Profiler button - had no way to follow a collapse it did not cause, so the two could disagree."
},

The chrome-hiding style tag also hides #profiler-icon.",

  "date": "2026-10-19T18:50:00Z",
  "type": "pr-merge",
  "pr": 134,
  "branch": "arena/d4ebc506-forge-engine",
  "base": "main",
  "title": "Browse the Phase 21 diagnostics in an interactive Inspector window (21.2–21.10)",
  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
  "modelVersion": null,
  "summary": "The remaining Phase 21 UI work in two halves. (1) The demo's floating Profiler panel draws the frame history: a category-stacked column per frame against the 60 Hz budget line with a lane chart of the selected frame's scopes, hover to select and click to pin; engine-side (engine/src/debug/frameTimeline.ts) it is pure geometry that charges every scope its self time and inherits an ancestor's category, so nested scopes are counted once and a host can draw it without a canvas. (2) The toolbar's Inspector button opens a floating window with one tab per diagnostic API — ECS, systems, render graph, GPU resources, physics, terrain, particles, streaming, world — each with a summary, a filter, a list and a detail pane, refreshing at 2 Hz while open and costing nothing while closed; rows are keyed so a selection survives a refresh by identity, detail is computed lazily for the selected row only, the list is rebuilt only when its contents change, and four tabs offer an opt-in debug-line overlay that the host's frame loop draws through Renderer.drawLine. Six inspector capabilities move to verified with the window as evidence; physics and particles stay partial (no contact-manifold overlay, no GPU particle readback) and diagnostics.inspectorPanel is partial for the window's own limits. The visible 21.10 console terminal remains open, so Phase 21 stays in progress. Rebases the closed PR #132's frame-profiler commits onto main rather than superseding them.",

  "file": "engine/src/terrain/trackGrading.ts",
  "what": "New TrackGradingGenerator pipeline stage (GradedCorridor, designBedProfile, canonical-JSON identity / fromIdentity): cuts a level, graded road bed into streamed terrain cells, grading every vertex from its own world position and natural height only.",
  "why": "TrackTerrain carves a height function, but TerrainWorld streams cells from a GeneratorPipeline, so a road in streamed terrain has to be cut into the cells. The Alpine rescue route ran over raw hillside with grades up to 87% and cross-slopes up to 62%, which no vehicle can use."
},
{

  "date": "2026-10-19T20:08:14Z",

  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",

  "file": "engine/src/terrain/pipelineSpec.ts",
  "what": "Registered a describable `track-grading` stage kind whose codec round-trips through TrackGradingGenerator.identity / fromIdentity.",
  "why": "TerrainWorld hashes its pipeline with describePipeline, which throws on a stage it does not know. The new stage has to be describable to be usable at all, to reach workers, and to change the cache key when the road changes."
},

  "why": "The route was a field of lumps. The bed is now designed from the natural height, so the ribbon, the terrain mesh and the vehicle's ground query agree inside the level core."

  "what": "New module: terrain pipeline (analytic RealisticHeightGenerator -> TrackGradingGenerator -> ClimateBiomeGenerator for slopes only), four-layer winter splat weights (snow / rock / scree / tundra from slope, curvature and noise), AlpineTerrainMaterial and createGradedHeight for build-time placement.",
  "why": "The old pipeline ran ThermalErosionGenerator (not seam-safe: neighbouring chunks disagreed along their border by up to ~6 m, right along the route's own chunk edge) and ValleyCarvingGenerator (isolated crater pits).   "summary": "Makes Alpine Search & Rescue (?scene=alpine-rescue) look and drive like a mountain rescue instead of a lump field with a box truck. Vehicle: the truck had no wheels - VehicleSystem writes world poses into wheel entities, which the scene had parented to the chassis, so they sat ~300 m away; wheels are now root entities, and the body is a lofted wagon with real wheel arches, roof rack, light bar and lathe-turned winter tyres (meshKit.ts, alpineRescueVehicle.ts). Terrain: the 320 m route ran over raw hillside with grades up to 87% and cross-slopes up to 62%. The new engine stage TrackGradingGenerator (describable through a track-grading codec with a canonical-JSON identity, so it reaches workers and the cache key) cuts a designed, grade-limited bed into every streamed chunk (worst cross-slope 0.2%, worst grade 10%, zero chunk-border mismatch), and the road ribbon is built from the same bed. The scene's pipeline no longer runs ThermalErosionGenerator (not seam-safe: chunk borders disagree by up to ~6 m, right along the route) or ValleyCarvingGenerator (isolated crater pits); both stages are unchanged and their caveats are written up in docs/TERRAIN-REALISTIC.md. The ground is a four-layer PBR splat (snow, rock, scree, tundra) with procedural normal-mapped textures. Snow: the z-fighting overlay mesh is replaced by the engine's weather snow, fed through a remapped shade because the engine shader saturates flat ground at cover ~0.43, with a sub-zero ALPINE_WEATHER set so snow lies instead of melting. Adds ?tier=low|medium|high and the __forge.rescuePlace / rescueSnowpack screenshot hooks; mission logic and every snapshot / DOM hook are unchanged. Six new suites (84 checks) plus new alpineSnowpack groups; the selrun catalog is now 152 suites / 1048 coverage claims. Rebased onto main at 4e4bf3a.",

{
  "id": "2129",
  "date": "2026-10-20T00:50:37Z",
  "type": "change",
  "pr": null,
  "branch": "arena/a658d556-forge-engine",
  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
  "modelVersion": null,
  "file": "engine/src/population/vegetation.ts",
  "what": "`VegetationModel` gains a third distance ring, `shadowDistance` (default `Infinity`): past it `refresh()` clears `castShadow` on the instance's parts. Adds `Instance.casting`, counts it in `stats_`/`stats()` (`casting`), resets it on `onDetach`, and documents the ring.",
  "why": "A forest's per-frame cost is its shadow pass. Casting is only readable close in, so it should stop well inside the draw distance - and a model with no ring keeps every part a caster forever."
},
{
  "id": "2130",
  "date": "2026-10-20T00:50:37Z",
  "type": "change",
  "pr": null,
  "branch": "arena/a658d556-forge-engine",
  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
  "modelVersion": null,
  "file": "engine/src/rendering/renderer.ts",
  "what": "`collectBatches` takes a fast path in `classifyAABB`: when the coarse plane test returns `PlaneTest.Inside` the AABB is fully inside the frustum, so the BVH intersection is skipped.",
  "why": "Most renderables in a populated scene are fully inside the frustum; only `Crossing` boxes need the tree. Cuts the per-frame cull cost of the vegetation-heavy demos."
},
{
  "id": "2131",
  "date": "2026-10-20T00:50:37Z",
  "type": "change",
  "pr": null,
  "branch": "arena/a658d556-forge-engine",
  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
  "modelVersion": null,
  "file": "engine/src/audio/vehicle.ts",
  "what": "`VehicleAudioOptions` gains `strokes?: 2 | 4`. `firingsPerRev = cylinders * (2/strokes)`, so a two-stroke fires every revolution; it also brightens the engine voice with rpm (+600 + 1400*rpmNorm), cuts roughness to 0.55, and puts an expansion-chamber ring at 4x the firing frequency on the whine voice above 42% of the rev range under throttle.",
  "why": "The off-road demo's quad is a two-stroke single, which sounds nothing like the four-stroke default. No nodes are added - the ring reuses the whine voice a four-stroke leaves free in forward gear, so the 12-source graph invariant holds."
},
{
  "id": "2132",
  "date": "2026-10-20T00:50:37Z",
  "type": "change",
  "pr": null,
  "branch": "arena/a658d556-forge-engine",
  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
  "modelVersion": null,
  "file": "engine/src/vehicles/vehicle.ts",
  "what": "`VehicleOptions` exposes `inertiaYaw`, `inertiaPitch`, `inertiaRoll`, `angularDamping`, `lsdBias`, `tcSlip`, `tcStrength`, `handbrakeTorque`, `suspensionRest`, `suspensionTravel`, `wheelInertia`, `maxSteerAngle` and `efficiency`; `createVehicleConfig` honours them. Every default is unchanged.",
  "why": "A 265 kg quad on a 1.28 m wheelbase cannot use a car's numbers: the mass-scaled inertias steer like a barge, and car-scale brake torque (4500 N.m on a 0.27 m tyre = 16.7 kN at a wheel carrying ~650 N) locks all four wheels the instant the pedal is touched."
},
{

  "branch": "arena/a658d556-forge-engine",

Also `QUAD_FRONT_TYRE_WIDTH` / `QUAD_REAR_TYRE_WIDTH` and `allQuadBodySources`.",
  "why": "The demo was carrying a UTV built from twelve boxes. A sport quad is a spine frame, a two-stroke with an expansion chamber, four independent arms, handlebars and fenders - authored off the ground plane so the seat height does not depend on the suspension length."

{

  "what": "Replaces the UTV with the two-stroke quad: `buildQuadSources` body and wheels (root entities, left wheels mirrored), a 421 cc two-stroke `EngineModel` (idle 1900, peak 46 N.m at 7600, redline 9500) behind a close-ratio five-speed `Transmission` (final 3.45, upshift 9000, downshift 5600), and a 265 kg config with its own inertias, damping, suspension, steer angle, brake torques, LSD bias and TC window. Rate-limits rider input (steer 4.2/s toward lock, 6.5/s back to centre; throttle 5.5/s up, 9/s down; brake 8/s, 10/s). Tightens the chase camera to 4.6 m back / 1.9 m up, makes the 'cab' view the rider's eye, adds rpm to the overlay, sets `VehicleAudio` to one cylinder / two strokes, and gives the forest real distance rings (trees 16/22/30 lod, 70/105/145 max, 26/38/52 shadow; bushes 45/70/100 + 28/38/48; shadow range 40/55/70; thinner backdrop scatter).",

Measured at the spawn on the mock GPU (high tier), visible renderables fell 6705 -> 2813 and shadow casters to 664; the quad now ramps into lock instead of darting, and its brakes modulate instead of grabbing."
},

{
  "id": "2149",
  "date": "2026-10-20T01:07:13Z",
  "type": "pr-merge",
  "pr": 137,
  "branch": "arena/a658d556-forge-engine",
  "base": "main",
  "title": "Off-road demo: a two-stroke quad, a forest that culls and stops casting at range, and handlebar-rate input",
  "model": "Arena Agent Mode",
  "modelVersion": null,
  "summary": "Replaces the off-road hill demo's UTV (?scene=offroad) with a 421 cc two-stroke sport quad, fixes the extreme lag when facing the treeline, and fixes the handling. Vehicle: new examples/src/scenes/offroadQuad.ts builds the machine from the mesh kit - spine frame, steering head, double A-arms, swingarm and solid rear axle, nerf bars and pegs, bumper hoop, rear rack, handlebars, lofted tank and beak fenders with arc-strip wings, the two-stroke's finned cylinder, and its expansion chamber lathed onto the pipe's own axis - plus two wheel assemblies (narrow front, wide rear: lathed carcass with chevron lugs, dished rim, inboard disc) built about their own origin with the axle along +X so VehicleSystem can pose them as root entities (left meshes yaw 180 deg so the dish faces outboard). Drivetrain: idle 1900, 46 N.m at 7600, limiter 9500, behind a close-ratio five-speed and a 3.45 final so every upshift lands the crank back inside the band. Sound: VehicleAudioOptions gains strokes?: 2|4 (firingsPerRev = cylinders * 2/strokes, brighter and less gritty, with an expansion-chamber ring at 4x the firing frequency on the whine voice a four-stroke leaves free in forward gear) - no new nodes, so the pinned 12-source graph holds. Lag: the forest was planted with maxDistance 0 (never culled) and both parts of every tree casting, so facing the trees drew ~6705 renderables with thousands of casters per cascade per frame; VegetationModel now has a third ring, shadowDistance (Instance.casting, counted in stats_.casting), Renderer.collectBatches skips the BVH refinement when classifyAABB says Inside, and the demo gives trees lod/max/shadow rings of 16/22/30, 70/105/145 and 26/38/52 m (bushes 45/70/100 + 28/38/48, thinner backdrop scatter, shadow range 40/55/70). Measured on the mock GPU at the spawn, high tier: visible renderables 6705 -> 2813, casters -> 664. Handling: rider input is rate-limited (steer 4.2/s toward lock, 6.5/s back to centre, throttle 5.5/s up and 9/s down, brake 8/s and 10/s) because digital keys gave instant full lock on a 1.28 m wheelbase; VehicleOptions exposes inertias, angularDamping, wheelInertia, suspensionRest/Travel, maxSteerAngle, handbrakeTorque, lsdBias, tcSlip, tcStrength and efficiency with every default unchanged, and the 265 kg quad uses them (78/42/26 kg.m^2, 0.4 rad of lock, 420/520/560 N.m of brakes - car-scale torque locked all four 0.27 m wheels the instant the pedal was touched - and a wider 0.18 TC window). Chase camera tightened to 4.6 m back / 1.9 m up, the cab view is the rider's eye, the overlay shows rpm, and the touch steering control is drawn as handlebars (maxAngle 45, returnRate 14). Also fixes two regressions PR #136 left on main: alpineRescueScene.vehicleState() returned fields the closed DemoSceneHandle shape does not have (npm run typecheck was failing, and npm test does not typecheck), and the Alpine rear-wheel-lock case called the private Vehicle.isRearWheel with an index, so its condition was always false and the lock was never asserted. Tests: a new 15-check suite over the whole off-road demo (tests/examples/offroadHillScene.test.ts - the demo had no coverage at all), the shadow ring in the vegetation suite, the two-stroke in the audio suite, and the light-machine options in the vehicle suite; the selrun catalog is now 153 suites / 1059 coverage claims. Gates green: build, typecheck, lint:arch, selrun check, docs:check, npm test (153/153) and check:wgsl.",
